facts.statement: Pseudocrypturus is an extinct genus of paleognathous bird.
facts.quote: Pseudocrypturus is a genus of extinct paleognathous bird.

facts.statement: Pseudocrypturus is related to modern ostriches.
facts.quote: It is a relative of such modern birds as ostriches.

facts.statement: The name Pseudocrypturus translates to 'false tinamou'.
The species name cercanaxius refers to the bird's rudimentary pygostyle.
facts.quote: The type species name, cercanaxius, comes from ancient Greek words , tail, and , worthless, in reference to the rudimentary pygostyle of the species.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Pseudocrypturus is held at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil is in the collection of the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History.

facts.statement: Pseudocrypturus fossils were found in the Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation in Wyoming.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Fossil Butte Member, Green River Formation, Lincoln County, Wyoming.

facts.statement: Pseudocrypturus belongs to the family Lithornithidae.
Pseudocrypturus lived during the Early Eocene.
Pseudocrypturus lived between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 51.1 million years ago)
